real_conflicts: The proposal to increase the font size and weight of the bottom text (typography_integration) risks creating a visual competition with the headline. If the bottom block becomes too heavy, it will disrupt the clear top-down visual path (Headline -> Spark -> Fire -> Action) and turn the bottom into a second focal point rather than a supporting base.
accepted: The proposal to increase vertical spacing (line-height) between the instructional lines (composition_hierarchy) is essential to stop the bottom text from looking like a cramped footer.

The proposal to add a subtle vertical gradient to the foreground (color_atmosphere_craft) is accepted because it helps integrate the bottom text into the landscape rather than having it float on a flat void, improving the overall spatial cohesion.
concession: I concede that the current bottom text is not just 'cramped' but actively failing as a compositional anchor due to the clipping of the 'National Forest Safety Initiative' line. This is a structural failure, not just a stylistic one.
compromise: We will increase the line-height of the three instructional lines to create a distinct, rhythmic stack. Simultaneously, we will apply the proposed subtle background gradient to the bottom third to lift the text off the black void, ensuring the 'National Forest Safety Initiative' line is fully visible and legible without needing to increase the font size to a level that would compete with the headline.
nonnegotiable: The central vertical axis connecting the headline, the spark, and the fire plume is the structural spine of the poster and must remain the dominant visual path.
